subject: ClearSight capacity stress test + burst-lane plan
content:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@clearsight.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot sizing ask: dedicated + burst lanes

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was encouraged by the latency numbers. We need to lock down committed capacity sizing for the pilot and procurement is asking for a short effects analysis: what committed dedicated pool would you recommend to meet our SLOs and what does the short-term burst lane look like for traffic spikes?

Quick context: our prod-like traffic sample (attached) shows regular steady-state at ~12k tokens/sec during business hours, with short spikes up to ~42k tokens/sec (1-3 minute windows) roughly 4–6x per day when new content is pushed. Target SLO is p95 inference latency < 350ms for the conversational flow (average response ~80 tokens, model = 13B offspring tuned).

Can you send a recommended committed slab (GPUs), a burst-lane strategy (how many spare GPUs and how fast to spin up), and the headroom % you’d recommend for safe rollouts? Also advise on how KV cache warmup affects the short spikes.

Appreciate it — can we get a draft by EOD next Friday (25th)?

— Sarah

---

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@clearsight.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask: dedicated + burst lanes

Sarah — thanks for the detail and the sample traffic. I ran a quick pass and attached an annotated capacity workbook with assumptions. High level summary below; more detail in the workbook.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Committed pool: 8 GPUs (dedicated slab) for steady-state.
- Burst-lane: additional 6 GPUs pre-warmed in a fast-burst pool (logical separate slab) to handle 2–3 minute spikes; autoscale to add another 4 GPUs if spike exceeds 2 minutes.
- Headroom: target 40% headroom above expected peak token/sec for safe rollouts and model upgrades.
- KV cache: pre-warming top 10% of request prefixes reduces p95 by ~80–120ms during bursts; recommend warmup job + short cache TTL for pilot.

Key reasoning: your steady-state (~12k tokens/sec) maps to ~2.4 GPUs at our measured 13B int8 throughput (~5k tokens/sec/GPU under realistic batching). We round up for redundancy and variance, and to hold latency SLO at p95 under the traffic distribution you shared. The bursts to ~42k tokens/sec would need ~8.4 GPUs raw — we recommend handling that primarily with a burst-lane (6 pre-warmed GPUs + autoscale margin) to keep committed spend predictable.

I'll outline the timeline for validation tests and a stress-run recipe — Ben and Aditya, feel free to add numbers or tweaks.

— Mina

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@clearsight.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask: dedicated + burst lanes

Mina — quick add from ops/throughput side: our bench for the tuned 13B (q4_0-like profile, contiguous KV hot set) is ~5.2k tok/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent GPU with batching tuned to your arrival distribution (we used a 150ms batching window for the test). That baseline is what Mina used above.

Some clarifying notes on the numbers in the workbook:
- We include a 1.25x fudge for in-flight variance (cold cache, model warming, occasional tail retries).
- Burst-lane pre-warmed pool should use the same model artifact and quant profile to avoid cold-warm transitions that increase latency by 250–400ms.
- For autoscale: scale-up target = add GPUs to get you to 1.5x the instantaneous token/sec observed in the last 30s window; scale decisions evaluated every 15s. This gives fast response without noisy churn.

Operationally: to hit p95 < 350ms during bursts we must ensure (a) warm model and warm KV cache on the burst GPUs, and (b) a routing rule that keeps long-tail requests on committed slab when we detect heavy contention.

— Ben

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@clearsight.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask: dedicated + burst lanes

Adding the math we used in the attached workbook (excerpt):
- Observed steady tokens/sec: 12,000 tok/s
- Observed spikes: 42,000 tok/s (peak short windows)
- Measured per-GPU throughput (13B, production mix): 5,200 tok/s

Committed GPUs (raw) = ceil(12,000 / 5,200) = 3 GPUs => add redundancy, scheduling headroom and SLO buffer => recommended 8 GPUs committed (includes replication for availability and room for canary testing).

Burst sizing: peak 42,000 / 5,200 = 8.1 GPUs. Recommended pattern: 6 GPUs pre-warmed (fast-burst), autoscale +4 if sustained over 90s. That gives effective max of 18 GPUs in extreme sustained cases (but you would only pay for autoscaled minutes).

Headroom rationale: 40% headroom accounts for imprecise batch efficiencies at varying payload sizes, client-side jitter, and experiment traffic. For pilot with tighter budget we can drop to 25% headroom but we expect higher p95 risk.

Test recipe (for next week):
1) Run 30m steady at 12k tok/s against committed pool and validate p95 < 350ms.
2) Run five stochastic bursts to 42k tok/s for 2–3 minutes and validate fallbacks (routing + cache warmup) keep p95 < 400ms across both pools.
3) Run a long-duration 10m sustained 1.5x peak to validate autoscale and billing profile.

I'll attach the validation scripts.

— Aditya

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@clearsight.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, procurement@clearsight.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask: dedicated + burst lanes

Team — this is super helpful. A few follow-ups from our side before we finalize the SOW: a) any guidance on token-counting differences between our instrumentation and Redwood's (we saw ~10% variance in the sample), b) can you note expected cost delta if we reduce committed GPUs from 8 -> 6 but rely more on burst minutes, and c) can the pre-warmed burst pool be limited to business hours?

Procurement also asked for a short note on expected billing profile during the 30-day pilot (expected committed hours vs autoscaled minutes) — can you include an example?

Thanks — Sarah

---

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@clearsight.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, procurement@clearsight.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask: dedicated + burst lanes

Sarah — answers inline below and attached a sample billing-profile tab in the workbook.

1) Token counting variance: measurement differences typically come from truncation rules, client-side chunking, and whether special tokens are counted. We normalize on server-side tokenization for contract purposes; historically discrepancies are within ±8–12% for mixed client stacks. We'll include a reconciliation script you can run against a 24h sample.

2) Cost delta: dropping committed from 8 -> 6 reduces committed monthly fixed cost by ~25% but increases expected autoscaled minutes during peaks. For your traffic mix we model an extra ~9k autoscaled GPU-minutes during the 30-day pilot (workbook sample). That maps to ~12–18% extra variable spend vs baseline committed 8 GPUs, but with higher p95 risk. I attached a simple pro forma showing the two profiles.

3) Time-limited burst pool: yes — we can gate the burst-lane to business hours with a rule set (09:00–19:00 local). Outside business hours bursts will either fail-over to a smaller shared pool (if enabled) or queue by priority.

Next steps:
- I’ll update the SOW draft with the recommended 8 GPU committed slab, burst-lane 6 pre-warmed + autoscale +4, and the headroom recommendation of 40%.
- Ops will run the three validation steps next Tue/Wed and share results.
- Procurement: we’ve attached a billing-example you can paste into the SOW appendix.

If you want a lower-cost pilot variant we can run a 6 GPU committed + 8 pre-warmed burst combination and show the tradeoffs in the test runs; it’s feasible but we’ll mark the SLO risk as medium.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
